title: Tulip Tree: Ancient Tulip Poplars You Can Visit
meta_description: The leaf looks as though someone cut the tip off with scissors. The Queens Giant, wild in a New York forest, is put at 350 to 450 years.
intro: You can identify it from the pavement: the leaf looks as though someone snipped the tip off with scissors, four lobes and a flat end where the point should be. Liriodendron tulipifera is a tree of the eastern United States, and there it grows wild and tall. The Queens Giant came up on its own in a stretch of Alley Pond Park's forest that was never cleared; New York dates it to at least 368 years, and it is the tallest carefully measured tree in the city. In Chapel Hill, campus legend says the University of North Carolina stands where General Davie fell asleep under one in 1792. Europe's oldest exist because of the post. On 1 October 1716 a London apothecary sent seed to Leiden, and Herman Boerhaave sowed it in the botanical garden where it still stands. Braga's, planted under João V, is called the largest in Portugal.
